log.text: Toxic Spikes up on P1's side
Toxic Spikes up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Dragapult outspeeds and OHKOs Noivern with Dragon Darts, pressures Toxapex with Shadow Ball. Incineroar provides Fake Out + Intimidate to disrupt early. Kingambit resists Boomburst, immune to Toxic Spikes, and scales with Supreme Overlord. Talonflame sets Tailwind for speed control and threatens Excadrill/Scizor with priority Flare Blitz via Gale Wings.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 win. Opponent: Toxapex (Leftovers, BanefulBunker/Recover/Haze/ToxicSpikes), Excadrill (LifeOrb/MoldBreaker, EQ/IronHead/RockSlide/StealthRock), Noivern (WiseGlasses/Infiltrator, Boomburst/DracoMeteor/Hurricane/Defog), Rotom-Wash (WacanBerry/Levitate, ShadowBall/VoltSwitch/WillOWisp/Protect), Scizor (ExpertBelt/Technician, BulletPunch/Uturn/BugBuzz/Superpower), Absol (FocusSash/Justified, SuckerPunch/KnockOff/CloseCombat/StoneEdge). Toxic Spikes threatens grounded non-Steel/Poison switches (Incineroar, Appletun, Serperior). Dragapult and Talonflame are key speed assets. Kingambit is a late-game anchor.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex leads to scout, set Toxic Spikes, and provide Regenerator sustainability. Rotom-Wash follows as a pivot with Ground immunity via Levitate and Volt Switch. Excadrill is the primary Kingambit and Incineroar answer with Mold Breaker Earthquake, kept in back for safe entry. Absol serves as the dedicated Kingambit revenge killer with priority Sucker Punch and Focus Sash, addressing the notebook's note about needing reliable finishing power. Noivern benched — explicitly inadequate vs Dragapult/DracoMeteor.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Parting Shot pivot core: Dragapult/Incineroar. Kingambit is primary closer — Supreme Overlord + Kowtow Cleave. Excadrill Mold Breaker Earthquake is best check. Toxic Spikes on foe side; second layer means bad poison on future switch-ins. Dragapult double-hit Dragon Darts punishes Water/Ground switch-ins. Foe Kingambit left at 23% not converted — need priority or secure KO before reset. Noivern inadequate vs this opponent; benched for game 2. One unrevealed slot still ambiguous (Appletun/Serperior/Talonflame). Absol Focus Sash Sucker Punch is key for Kingambit revenge kill.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out Rotom-Wash to prevent Shadow Ball on Dragapult. Dragon Darts targets Rotom-Wash: if Rotom Protects, both hits redirect to Toxapex (37-69%); if Toxapex Baneful Bunkers, both hits land on Rotom (51-96%) + Fake Out chip (10-18%) for a KO chance. Either way Dragapult stays safe and we deal meaningful damage.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult Dragon Darts KOs Rotom-Wash before it moves (51-96% min into 18% HP). If Rotom Protects, it lives but wastes its turn. Incineroar Parting Shot into Toxapex stacks -2 Atk/-1 SpA, then pivots to Talonflame. Next turn: priority Tailwind via Gale Wings. This line generates value whether Rotom Protects or not, and Toxapex can't threaten with -2 Atk.

Dragapult stays in to threaten Rotom-Wash (Shadow Ball KOs 18% HP Rotom) and pressure Toxapex. Incineroar switches to Kingambit: Steel typing grants Toxic Spikes immunity, Dark STAB hits both foes neutrally, Sucker Punch provides priority, and it preserves Talonflame's Gale Wings for later speed control. Kingambit also serves as a late-game Supreme Overlord anchor.

Kingambit Kowtow Cleave into Toxapex: 34-60% chip while Toxapex likely Recovers or Hazes. If Rotom Protects (low success after last-turn use), Kingambit still pressures Toxapex. Double-targeting different foes avoids overkill waste.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult Protects to dodge EQ; Kingambit switches to Talonflame, which is immune to both Ground (EQ) and Toxic Spikes. This blanks the likely Baneful Bunker + EQ turn. Next turn Talonflame sets priority Tailwind at full HP with Gale Wings, giving us a decisive Speed edge. Stealth Rock is a risk (50% to Talonflame) but EQ is far more probable given the board; even if rocks go up, Talonflame still outspeeds Excadrill to set Tailwind.

Recover brings Toxapex from 16% to ~43%, which is the only way to survive both Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave (25.5-30.6%) and Talonflame's Brave Bird (30.6-36.3%). At 16%, any attacking move KO's; at 43%, Toxapex lives through either hit and can continue pivoting. Rotom-Wash is fainted so must pass.

reflections.summary: We won the game and series 2-0 because our offensive pressure overwhelmed the opponent's passive Toxapex stall. Bringing Kingambit, immune to Toxic Spikes, and Talonflame's priority Brave Bird allowed us to break through Baneful Bunker and Recover while eliminating their other threats quickly. The opponent's Toxapex lacked any attacking moves, making it a non-factor once isolated. Our team composition had strong synergy, and we executed without errors, maintaining momentum throughout.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, consider bringing a Taunt user (e.g., Scrafty or Mega Gardevoir from the full roster) to completely shut down Toxapex's stall moves. Alternatively, Appletun could pressure Rotom-Wash and Excadrill, but beware of Toxic Spikes. The current four brought worked well, but adding Taunt would make the matchup even more lopsided. Also, plan for potential Scizor or Noivern if the opponent adjusts their brought Pokémon.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's Toxapex is pure stall (Baneful Bunker, Recover, Haze, Toxic Spikes; no attacks). It frequently uses Baneful Bunker consecutively. Excadrill is Mold Breaker Life Orb with Stealth Rock; it will Earthquake even with ally Absol (Focus Sash). Absol is Sash Justified with Sucker Punch, Knock Off, Close Combat, Stone Edge. Rotom-Wash is Wacan Berry with Will-O-Wisp, Volt Switch, Shadow Ball, Protect. Noivern (Wise Glasses, Infiltrator) and Scizor (Expert Belt, mixed) were not brought this series but may appear in rematches. Opponent prioritizes early Toxic Spikes. Kingambit is immune to Toxic Spikes and pressures Toxapex. Talonflame's priority Brave Bird is effective but gets poisoned on switch-in. Incineroar's Intimidate and Fake Out are valuable. Dragapult provides fast special damage. In future, Taunt shuts down Toxapex entirely; consider hazard control or accept poison. Be ready for possible Scizor or Noivern adjustments.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 in a series where the team preview plan was the primary issue. The four chosen (Rotom-Wash, Toxapex, Excadrill, Absol) lacked the offensive firepower and dedicated Kingambit answers needed against an opponent running Dragapult/Incineroar pivot + Kingambit closer + Gale Wings Talonflame. Toxapex was a competent defensive anchor but the team had no way to break through opposing Kingambit boosts (Supreme Overlord) or threaten offensively. Rotom-Wash was a dead pick with Wacan Berry (weakens one of its own STAB types) and a purely defensive Calm spread that contributed zero damage all game. Excadrill was frail enough that Dragapult's Shadow Ball 2HKO'd it and it never got a clean sweep. Absol's Focus Sash was burned by a Gale Wings Brave Bird on turn 5. Noivern and Scizor — both left on the bench — could have provided priority (Scizor Bullet Punch) or hazard control (Noivern Defog) that were sorely needed. The opponent's Kingambit was never adequately checked; Toxapex survived only via Baneful Bunker cycling and Regenerator. The game was unwinnable once Toxapex finally fell to a critical Brave Bird on turn 10 followed by the finishing Brave Bird on turn 11. Noivern and Scizor should have been considered for the six, and at minimum Scizor's priority would have given a reliable Kingambit answer.
reflections.adjustment: 1) Re-evaluate Rotom-Wash: replace Wacan Berry with Assault Vest or Leftovers; consider dropping it entirely for a more offensive team member. 2) Bring Scizor over one of the current six — Bullet Punch is essential as a Kingambit check and priority user. 3) Consider Weavile or Mamoswine for Ice Shard priority revenge kills on Dragapult and to threaten opposing Dragons. 4) Build Excadrill as a cleaner rather than a lead — pair it with a dedicated pivot that can bring it in safely after Intimidate or Parting Shot. 5) Absol is too frail for this matchup; replace with a bulkier physical attacker or a dedicated Dragapult check. 6) Against this specific opponent, prioritize hard-hitting attackers and priority users over balanced pivots — Toxapex alone cannot win games without offensive support.
reflections.notebook: Opponent pivot core: Dragapult / Incineroar with Parting Shot. Kingambit is the closer — Supreme Overlord stacks make Kowtow Cleave lethal in late game; need priority or hard counters (Scizor, Weavile, strong neutral hits). Talonflame with Gale Wings + Sharp Beak Brave Bird is an immediate threat especially after Tailwind; Intimidate from Incineroar compounds physical damage. Opponent did not bring Appletun or Serperior this game — may be hidden surprise picks or situational; do not assume they are dead weight. Toxic Spikes: opponent layers them freely; Toxapex is immune and useful as their primary check. Rotom-Wash with Wacan Berry was a poor choice — item weakens own STAB, Calm spread too passive; rework or replace. Excadrill Mold Breaker Earthquake is strong in theory but frail vs Dragapult Shadow Ball; needs safer entry. Noivern and Scizor were unused — both have roles (Defog, priority) that were missing. Key takeaway: this opponent's team rewards fast, hard-hitting offense and punishes passive/balanced play; prep accordingly with priority and wallbreakers.
